plumbing.summary: Everything passed: gofmt, go vet, the tests of every package the change touches, and every acceptance test.
plumbing.review:
Three changes are needed:

- **[P2] CI uses the wrong baseline to identify new tests.** [scope.go:351](scope.go:351) inventories the current base tip, while changed paths come from `base...head`. If base independently deletes an existing unnamed test, a branch modifying that test is incorrectly admitted as adding a new regression file. Use the merge-base inventory consistently and cover diverged branches.

- **[P2] Planned package deletion now fails checks.** [sandbox.go:159](sandbox.go:159) uses `GoPackages`, which treats planned `.go` paths as establishing packages even after deletion. Removing an obsolete package therefore runs `go test ./removedpkg`, which fails. Determine executable test packages from files present in the candidate.

- **[P2] Formatting checks now include protected, unchanged tests.** [sandbox.go:178](sandbox.go:178) includes every test in each touched package. An existing unformatted unnamed test now blocks the build, although staging prevents the builder from correcting it. Restrict the added formatting coverage to admitted new regression files.

The supplied checks pass, and acceptance sources match the ratified plan. Their coverage misses these cases. The repair lifecycle and accounting otherwise look sound; I found no test-specific shortcuts, added network/host access, secret exposure, or material style mismatch.

**Merger work:** record issue #281’s new policies and complete required Docker/network checks unavailable here.

VERDICT: changes needed — fix baseline classification, deleted-package selection, and formatting scope, with regression coverage.
